meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen saw a zero on his phone in the middle of class. Explain that.

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Now the zero itself: on what basis?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. Owen wrote it over the weekend and pasted it in, which is what a paste looks like. Turn the screen so I can see it myself.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up. And a paste at 11:52 tells you nothing about where he wrote it, so what else do you have?
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Students misquote all the time, so where else could that line have come from: a study guide, a film, an edition you don't use? And the screen, Hale.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay; that's what an outline is for. You've described three things and shown me none of them. Hand me the outline and the essay.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
Being stuck is what paralysis means. A seventeen-year-old cornered after class, and your own notes of it, are not evidence I can check. Four things now, and I'm still holding nothing.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in class against a weekend at home, of course it's cleaner. Five things, Hale, and not one page across this table. Put something in my hand or I'm going to the principal.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good, because I have the vendor's own guide in my bag saying exactly that. Now stop listing and show me.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

That's 4.4, and I'll want it in writing tonight. But you're offering a rewrite on evidence you've only read aloud to me. Show me the pages, and tell me where and in front of whom this rewrite happens.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Ten minutes. Not until I've seen with my own eyes what it rests on. Turn the screen to me, Hale.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
No day suits him yet. You keep booking dates around evidence you won't let me see. One page, now.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
No. I've agreed to nothing except that you'll put 4.4 in writing tonight. You've read me five things and handed me none, so the zero still stands on your word alone.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
The version history and the essay, in front of me, now. Until I've seen them, the zero comes off and this goes to the principal.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to put in writing a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require to see the version history and the essay itself, and until I have, I expect the zero withdrawn. You said I would have this in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her fallback position; she accepted that 4.4 in writing protects his record but agreed to no rewrite, and she still wants to see your documents and the zero withdrawn until she has, so this is close to the fair outcome of a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record but not there yet.
What moved her: You put procedure 4.4 on the table correctly and committed to it privately and in writing, which met her demand about his record.
What cost ground: You described all six pieces of evidence without ever showing her one or answering her defences, so none of them counted and she never reached her last position.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its edits between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before the essay was due, came very close to that night; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she pushed back on the version history by saying he pasted in a weekend draft, turn your screen to her right then and answer that point before you move on to the quotation.
